{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-de-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"67730f12222e222a18e30c684db96cd5de47f2cd67c0844c47db60af261943a1","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-de-class-d:lineage:55","source_registry_sha256":"7b6c7aeec232df29a8679bf39181604be2d91ce9a1cb4fcc709fed49cbe724bb","source_liveness_sha256":"53bd779b9965bd9d51630c8d8d055ccdc52a4d8ec7117a3b87241fc5129eb44f"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Vehicle preparation, restraint use and traffic-stop procedure","heading":"C2 — Vehicle preparation, restraint use and traffic-stop procedure","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Vehicle preparation, restraint use and traffic-stop procedure

FACT_ID: sec12-R01 | anchor: A05
A safety belt helps a driver stay behind the steering wheel during a side impact or abrupt turn and retain control. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec12-R02 | anchor: A05
Safety belts remain necessary in an airbag-equipped vehicle because belts and airbags are intended to work together. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec12-R03 | anchor: A05
The NHTSA and AAP recommendations reproduced in the handbook say children younger than one should always use a rear-facing car seat. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec12-R04 | anchor: A05
Infant-only seats are rear-facing; convertible and all-in-one seats commonly allow rear-facing use to higher size limits. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec12-R05 | anchor: A05
For ages one through three, the reproduced recommendation keeps a child rear-facing until the seat maker’s rear-facing height or weight limit is reached, then moves to a forward-facing harness. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec12-R06 | anchor: A06
The reproduced recommendation keeps children ages eight through twelve in boosters until an adult belt fits correctly, with continued use of the back seat. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec12-R07 | anchor: A06
Correct belt fit places a snug lap belt on the upper thighs, not the abdomen, and a snug shoulder belt across the shoulder and chest rather than the face or neck. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec12-R08 | anchor: A06
Choose a car seat that fits both the child and vehicle and can be used correctly every time. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec12-R09 | anchor: A06
Never put a rear-facing child seat ahead of an active frontal airbag. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec12-R10 | anchor: A06
A harness should be snug enough that excess webbing cannot be pinched at the child’s collarbone. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec12-R11 | anchor: A06
Position the harness chest clip level with the child’s armpits. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec12-R12 | anchor: A06
At the belt path, an installed car seat should move no more than one inch forward/backward or side-to-side under moderate checking force. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec12-R13 | anchor: A06
Use the top tether whenever possible for forward-facing installation, whether using lower anchors or the vehicle belt. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec12-R14 | anchor: A06
Never carry an unrestrained child on your lap; use an appropriate child seat. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec12-R15 | anchor: A06
Read both the vehicle manual and child-seat manual for correct installation and use. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec12-R16 | anchor: A07
Do not leave children or animals alone in a hot vehicle. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec12-R17 | anchor: A07
A belt can help prevent being knocked unconscious in a crash, which can improve the chance of escaping afterward. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec12-R18 | anchor: A07
Safety belts help prevent ejection into another vehicle’s path. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec12-R19 | anchor: A07
In a side impact, unrestrained occupants can slide toward the impact point rather than away from it. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec12-R20 | anchor: A08
An officer can initiate a traffic stop with visible or audible signals such as emergency lights or a siren and may approach from either side. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0112]

FACT_ID: sec12-R21 | anchor: A08
During a traffic stop, the officer may identify themself and their agency and state the reason for the stop. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0112]

FACT_ID: sec12-R22 | anchor: A08
The officer will request the driver’s license, insurance proof and registration during a traffic stop. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0112]

FACT_ID: sec12-R23 | anchor: A08
Driver and passengers should stay inside the vehicle unless the officer instructs otherwise. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0112]

FACT_ID: sec12-R24 | anchor: A08
When emergency lights appear behind you, remain calm, signal and pull off or aside as soon as safely possible, using the right side when possible. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0112]

FACT_ID: sec12-R25 | anchor: A08
After stopping for the officer, switch off the ignition and radio, stay inside unless told to exit and keep the hands visible on the wheel. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0112]

FACT_ID: sec12-R26 | anchor: A09
During the stop, remain attentive, avoid mobile-device use and sudden movements, and wait for instructions before reaching for documents. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0113]

FACT_ID: sec12-R27 | anchor: A09
Inform the officer at first contact if weapons are present in the vehicle. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0113]

FACT_ID: sec12-R28 | anchor: A09
At night, the officer may shine a spotlight toward the stopped vehicle. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0113]

FACT_ID: sec12-R29 | anchor: A09
For a compliment or complaint about an officer, contact the officer’s agency using that agency’s stated channels. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0113]

FACT_ID: sec12-R30 | anchor: A09
Consult the owner’s manual for starting and apply the parking brake before starting the vehicle. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0113]

FACT_ID: sec12-R31 | anchor: A09
For starting a manual-transmission vehicle, select neutral; some vehicles also require depressing the clutch. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0113]

FACT_ID: sec12-R32 | anchor: A09
For starting an automatic-transmission vehicle, select Park. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0113]

FACT_ID: sec12-R33 | anchor: A09
Accelerate smoothly and gradually because an abrupt start can spin the driven wheels and cause a slide, especially on slippery pavement. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0113]

FACT_ID: sec12-R34 | anchor: A09
Practice coordinating the clutch and accelerator so a manual-shift engine does not stall or over-rev during shifts. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0113]

FACT_ID: sec12-R35 | anchor: A09
Hold the steering wheel with hands on opposite sides, with the left between eight and ten o’clock and the right between two and four. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0113]

FACT_ID: sec12-R36 | anchor: A09
Look well ahead and to both road sides for situations needing steering so adjustments can be smooth. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0113]

FACT_ID: sec12-R37 | anchor: A09
The handbook recommends hand-over-hand steering for sharp corners and manually straightening the wheel after the turn rather than letting it slide through the fingers. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0113]
